The shared lowest common ancestor between Hydroxocobalamin and Amn, as well as between Cyanocobalamin and Amn, points to a broader network of interactions involving nitrogen-containing molecules, possibly through the Cobalamin (cbl, Vitamin B12) transport and metabolism pathway. The evidence from both paths supports a mechanism where Hydroxocobalamin may influence Amn via a chain of interactions involving Cobalamins, possibly through a shared metabolic or transport pathway. The integration of these findings highlights a possible functional link between Hydroxocobalamin and Amn, mediated by Cobalamins and nitrogen-containing entities.
